ambiguities.description: The chunk directs inquiries to a contact but the contact's name, email and phone are cut off, so bidders cannot tell to whom and by what channel questions must be sent.

The module list is presented as the City's current Tyler Technologies configuration, not explicitly as required functionality of the new system; a bidder would ask whether all listed modules (including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and approvals) must be replaced one-for-one.

The text states the City currently has five users but does not say whether five is the licensed user count required in the new system or whether growth must be accommodated; a bidder would ask for the required user licensing quantity.

The schedule says the City will make every effort to adhere to it, so it is unclear whether the proposal submission deadline of August 28, 2025 and the interview date are firm or may shift; a bidder would ask whether dates are binding and how changes will be communicated.

The RFP does not define what counts as a trade secret or how the City will treat marked information, so a bidder cannot tell which technical or pricing-adjacent content is safe to mark; the bidder would ask what criteria the City applies and whether marking affects evaluation.

The City's standard contract with terms and conditions is only 'available upon request', so bidders cannot see the terms they must accept before submitting; the bidder would ask for a copy of the standard contract and whether it will be attached as an exhibit.

The text says the City may leave open later negotiation and amendment of specific contract provisions, yet also states that any modified terms submitted with a proposal will be disregarded and can render the proposal nonresponsive; the bidder would ask how exceptions can be raised without risking rejection.

The text requires modification requests to be raised "during the question period" per Section 2.3, but the dates and procedure of that question period are not given here; a bidder would ask for the question-period deadline and the required format for submitting a proposed modification.

The City states it may exercise discretion not to consider any proposed modifications, without saying whether or how a Respondent is notified of the outcome before the proposal deadline; a bidder would ask whether acceptance of a requested modification will be confirmed before proposals are due.

The text allows exceptions for "general inquiries before submission and after status updates" but does not define who may be contacted, through what channel, or what counts as a general inquiry versus a prohibited communication; a bidder would ask which contact point and topics are permitted during the evaluation period.

The disqualification exception turns on the City's subjective judgment that a communication is "harmless and unintentional" and in the City's best interest, with no process for the respondent to explain or cure a communication; a bidder would ask whether there is a notice-and-cure procedure.

The City may reject any proposal on the basis of "fit, form, and function" without defining those terms, so bidders cannot tell what would disqualify a proposal beyond cost and stated specifications; the bidder would ask what criteria define fit, form and function.

The criterion "Technical support during software implementation and ongoing" is truncated and does not say what is evaluated (response times, support hours, staffing, cost) or what period "ongoing" covers; a bidder would ask what content and service levels must be described under this 25% criterion.

The text says submissions deemed noncompliant or technically unqualified will not be considered but does not define the compliance or qualification threshold; a bidder would ask what minimum qualifications or compliance checklist determines disqualification.

The text says no single requirement automatically disqualifies a respondent, yet non-compliance with any individual requirement may lead the City to reject a proposal entirely; a bidder would ask which requirements are pass/fail and how partial compliance is scored.

The page limit is stated as "should not exceed 20 pages" (desired) while the surrounding text says respondents are "required to adhere" to the guidelines; it is unclear whether exceeding 20 pages (plus allowances) makes a proposal non-compliant. The bidder would ask whether the 20-page limit is a pass/fail requirement.

The hard copy must be "received" at the address by the deadline, but the text does not say whether the mailed PO Box copy and the street-address copy are alternatives or whether both must be sent; it also does not state whether the hard copy may arrive after the email timestamp. The bidder would ask which address to use and whether the hard copy must physically arrive by 4:00 PM PST on August 28, 2025.

The text allows post-opening withdrawal only for "good cause" without defining what qualifies, so a bidder cannot tell whether a mistake or changed circumstances would be accepted; the bidder would ask what criteria the City applies to "good cause".

The text refers to "the required elements outlined below" and "additional details required for each proposal section" that are not contained in this chunk, so a bidder cannot tell from this text what the full set of required proposal elements is; the bidder would ask for the complete list of required proposal sections and their contents.

It is unclear who qualifies as an "authorized signature" (e.g., an officer of the firm, a specific title, or a notarized signatory) and which attachments require one; the bidder would ask what signatory authority and form of signature are acceptable.

The text does not say whether the listed response elements are mandatory or merely suggested, since the lead-in only says respondents "should" address the goals; a bidder would ask whether omitting any element (e.g., virtual demos) makes the proposal non-responsive.

It is unclear what "account number customization abilities" covers (customer-defined account numbering scheme, format, length, or numbering of the vendor's own accounts), which affects how the design and demo are presented.

The July 1, 2026 go-live is stated as the City's goal, not a contractual deadline, and no implementation start date or contract award date is given, so the bidder cannot size the implementation schedule; the bidder would ask whether July 1, 2026 is a firm requirement and when implementation is expected to begin.

The text does not say whether the account manager is required or merely an option, nor whether that role must be dedicated or on-site; the bidder would ask what level of account management commitment is expected.

The chunk refers to "this information" without defining what firm information and qualifications must be provided for each company; the bidder would ask what specific items (licenses, references, financials, resumes) are required per firm.

The City expresses a "desire" for participation by minority-, women-, disabled- and small-business enterprises but sets no goal, percentage, or required form of evidence, so a bidder cannot tell whether a specific subcontracting commitment or documentation is expected.

The text does not define what counts as "recent" experience (e.g., within the last three or five years), which affects which references and projects the bidder can cite; the bidder would ask for the cutoff period.

It is unclear what qualifies as a "local referral" (within the City of Colfax area, the county, or the region) and whether the in-person demonstration is a scored expectation; the bidder would ask for the geographic definition and whether the demonstration is required at bid time or later.

The text requires reimbursable expenses to be capped but does not state a cap amount or whether the City sets a maximum; a bidder would ask what cap level is acceptable or whether the cap is at the Respondent's discretion.

The text requires an estimate of costs/fees for "additional applications and/or vendors" without defining which applications or vendors are contemplated; a bidder would ask what additional applications/vendors must be priced.

The required insurance types are open-ended ("including, but not limited to") and no minimum coverage limits or additional-insured requirements are stated here, so the bidder cannot price the coverage; the bidder would ask which coverages and limits are required.

Attachment G asks for documentation of financial-data protection and secure access controls without naming a standard, framework or format, so the bidder cannot tell what evidence will be accepted; the bidder would ask which standard or format the documentation must follow.

The chunk refers to "required items" and "optional items" in the scope of work without identifying them here; a bidder would ask which deliverables are mandatory versus optional, since that determines the proposal content and price.

The scope does not say whether the 12 months of post-implementation support is included in the base price or is a separately priced option, nor when that period starts (go-live vs. contract signature). The bidder would ask how to price and schedule it.

The text does not define the volume or format of the prior 5 years of data to be imported, nor who supplies and cleans it. The bidder would ask for data volumes, source systems and file formats to size the migration effort.

The July 1, 2026 completion date is stated as a "goal" rather than a firm deadline, so it is unclear whether it is a binding milestone subject to penalties or an aspirational target; the bidder would ask whether the date is mandatory.

The project start is described only as "soon after awarding the contract and finalizing negotiations," leaving the start date and any notice-to-proceed period undefined; the bidder would ask for the expected award date and contract start date to build the schedule.

The text requires a capped reimbursable expense amount but gives no ceiling or basis for the cap, so bidders cannot tell whether the City expects a specific maximum or a respondent-proposed figure; the bidder would ask whether a maximum cap value or methodology is prescribed.

It is unclear how the 'Total price proposal' differs from the 'Total price for all services and deliverables' plus the reimbursable cap, i.e. whether the total price proposal is their sum or a separate figure; the bidder would ask how the three amounts relate.

The references must be for "similar services ... as outlined herein", but this chunk does not define what counts as similar; the bidder would ask what scope or service categories qualify as similar references.

The form requires written notice of relocation outside the United States but sets no timeframe or recipient, so a bidder cannot tell whether notice must precede the move and to whom it must be addressed.

The certification lists the same audit-opinion statement twice, so it is unclear whether both boxes must be checked or whether one is a drafting duplicate; the bidder would ask which representation is required.

The certification does not define what counts as a "material change" triggering the 15-day notice, nor whether the notice obligation continues after contract award; the bidder would ask for the standard to apply.

The required coverage limits, additional-insured status and certificate form for the workers compensation and commercial general liability policies are not stated, so the bidder cannot price the insurance or know whether its current coverage qualifies; the bidder would ask what limits and endorsements are required.

The text does not specify what form or level of detail the documentation of financial-data protection and access controls must take (e.g., policies, certifications, diagrams), nor which financial data or systems are in scope, so a bidder cannot judge what evidence will be accepted.

Conflicting requirements R099 and R139: One requires notice to the City within 30 days of material changes to the financial certification, while the other requires notice to the Contract Lead within 15 days.

client_situation.text: The City of Colfax, California — a Sierra Nevada foothills town of just under 2,000 people in Placer County at the junction of Interstate 80 and State Route 174 — is the issuing body and sole beneficiary of this RFP.
The City runs on annual budgeted revenues of $6 million with 11 full-time employees (one position vacant) plus one part-time/seasonal/contract employee, and its fiscal year ends June 30.

The City currently uses Tyler Technologies' Fund Balance fund accounting software with modules for Accounts Payable (including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and purchase orders with approvals), Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing and Business Licensing, and has five users.

The City is replacing its current system with a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting system because it wants a streamlined package that captures financial transactions systematically, supports budgeting and forecasting, produces reports and analysis for decision-making, and maintains auditable records.
The City's small staff size and single-vacancy headcount mean the selected vendor must carry substantial implementation and support workload rather than relying on City capacity.

goal.text: The City wants a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting software system plus complete support for initial implementation and ongoing services for all applications the selected vendor provides.
The City's stated go-live target is July 1, 2026, to align with the start of its new fiscal year, with the project starting soon after contract award and negotiation.

The scope is organized into four tasks: Task 1 Approach & Project Management Plan (weekly progress/budget/timeline meetings, dedicated project manager, audit and reporting expertise, recommended account structure), Task 2 Software Installation & Implementation (financial report writing, import of the prior 5 years of data, coordination with Accounting and IT to minimize disruption), Task 3 Staff Training During Implementation (personalized power-user training and manuals, at least one recorded session and manual for all staff, support for the first 12 months), and Task 4 Ongoing Technical Assistance & Support (automated updates and change notices, annual 1099/W-2 e-filing support, help desk or ticketing system).

Respondents must supply an implementation plan and timeline, describe support levels for implementation and for recurring licenses and services, name key implementation personnel, describe training by license level (in person, virtual or recorded), and describe the client engagement approach including use of an account manager.

Tab 1 requires a completed Attachment F "Software Abilities and Requirements" spreadsheet, identification of license types by level of use, a description of account number customization, disclosure of where other applications or vendors will be used, and the availability of virtual product demos.

success_criteria.text: Proposals are scored on four weighted criteria: 45% response to project goals and scope, 25% technical support during implementation and ongoing, 20% fee proposal and implementation schedule, and 10% information, qualifications and references.
Written questions are due July 31, 2025, the City posts its answers on www.colfax-ca.gov by August 14, 2025, and proposals are due August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST.
Finalists are notified September 11, 2025, virtual finalist interviews (if needed) are held September 25, 2025, and selection and contract award are targeted for October 22, 2025.
Proposals must include at least three references for similar services with valid e-mail addresses, and a missing or invalid email may cause rejection of the proposal.
The City prefers at least one local referral that can host an in-person software demonstration.
The City may shortlist finalists for interviews with City leadership or select without interviews, and price proposals cannot be altered or modified during clarification.
The City may reject any proposal on fit, form, function or cost, may make separate awards for different items, may not award certain items, or may cancel the RFP entirely.

constraints.text: Proposals must be one signed original hard copy plus one digital copy, no more than 20 pages plus 2 pages for the cover letter and 5 pages for appendices, emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov with the subject line "Accounting and Financial Software Submission" and the hard copy received by the same August 28, 2025 4:00 PM PST deadline at Attn: Shanna Stahl, PO Box 702, Colfax, CA 95713 or 33 S. Main Street, Colfax, CA 95713.
Late proposals and FAX submissions will not be accepted or evaluated.

The City will not accept unlimited reimbursable expenses; all reimbursable expenses must be capped in the Attachment A price proposal, which must break out implementation fees, recurring fees, license fees, support costs during versus after implementation, and estimated costs for additional applications or vendors.
Respondents must submit Attachment C disclosing all work locations and any use of workers outside the United States, which the City will weigh for additional risks and costs before award.

Respondents must submit Attachment D Certification of Financial Condition (stable finances, unqualified audit opinion, no IRS or government liens, current on taxes, no disqualifying litigation) and Attachment E proof of insurance including workers compensation and commercial general liability.
Attachment G requires documentation of measures protecting financial data and the secure access controls implemented.

Attachment F is an Excel spreadsheet the City provides as a separate document that must be completed and returned with the submission, and the City's standard contract for services is a separate document respondents must obtain and review.

Any additional or modified terms and conditions submitted with a proposal will be rejected and not evaluated, and objections to the City's terms stated in the proposal will be disregarded or cause rejection, so exceptions must be raised as written questions by July 31, 2025.

solution.summary: The bid delivers a hosted, cloud-based accounting and financial reporting platform for the City of Colfax, configured to replace the City's current Tyler Technologies Fund Balance modules (Accounts Payable with 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and approvals, Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing and Business Licensing) for five users, plus a full implementation services wrap. Delivery runs in four phases mirroring the RFP's task structure: an approach and project-management phase (dedicated project manager, weekly progress/budget/timeline meetings, audit-aware account structure recommendation), a build-and-migrate phase (configuration, financial report writing, import of five years of history, coordination with Accounting and IT), a training phase (power-user and all-staff training with manuals and at least one recorded session), and a twelve-month post-go-live support phase (help desk, automated update notices, annual 1099/W-2 e-filing support). The work is a build-and-configure engagement on a vendor-hosted subscription, not a custom software development, and is sequenced to reach the City's July 1, 2026 go-live at the start of its fiscal year. The team is a named implementation project manager, functional consultants per module, a report-writing specialist, a data migration engineer, a trainer, and an account manager who carries the relationship through renewal. A governance and compliance workstream runs alongside delivery to carry the RFP's contractual, insurance, certification, pricing-breakout and disclosure obligations, and the proposal itself is assembled to the RFP's required tab order and page limits.

components.title: Project management, governance and compliance obligations
components.description: A dedicated project manager runs the engagement with a written personnel management plan naming the PM, technical staff and their roles, and holds weekly meetings that track progress, budget and timeline against a published schedule. The same workstream owns the RFP's contractual and administrative obligations: no additional or modified terms are submitted with the proposal and no attempt is made to alter or delete the bar on modified terms; the team observes the no-contact rule during evaluation and accepts that a violation disqualifies it; it accepts that all RFP terms are enforceable contract conditions and that 'shall', 'must' and 'requirements' are binding; it notifies the City within 30 days of any condition materially altering the financial certification and notifies the Contract Lead within 15 days of material changes to the financial-condition representations; and it gives written notice if personnel relocate outside the United States. The bid team also files written questions by July 31, 2025, holds September 25, 2025 for virtual finalist interviews, and absorbs all proposal and interview costs without reimbursement.

claims.text: The City's fiscal year ends June 30, which is why the go-live target is July 1, 2026.
The City has 11 full-time employees with one position vacant plus one part-time/seasonal/contract employee, so the vendor must carry most implementation workload.

components.title: Hosted accounting and financial reporting platform
components.description: A cloud-hosted subscription platform configured to cover every module the City uses today: Accounts Payable including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and purchase orders with approval routing; Accounts Receivable; General Ledger; Payroll; Utility Billing; and Business Licensing. Transactions post systematically through the general ledger with budgeting and forecasting tools, and the reporting layer produces standard and ad hoc reports and analysis for Council and management decision-making. The system retains transaction detail, approval trails and documentation so records remain auditable for future reference, and it is licensed for the City's five users with a documented path to add licenses as staffing changes. The proposal identifies license types by level of use and states where any additional application or third-party vendor is used to meet a requirement.

claims.text: The City currently runs Tyler Technologies Fund Balance with Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing and Business Licensing modules and five users.

components.title: Account structure design and financial report writing
components.description: Consultants with public-sector audit and reporting expertise review the City's current chart of accounts and recommend an account structure that supports auditable reporting, fund accounting and the City's budget-to-actual and financial statement needs. The team then writes the City's financial reports in the new system, including the standard reports the City produces today and the analysis views its decision-makers rely on, and documents the numbering scheme and customization options so the City can maintain the structure itself. Account number customization is described concretely in the proposal: segment definitions, format and length, and how the City can define and change its own numbering.

components.title: Data migration of five years of history
components.description: The team extracts, maps, cleans and loads the prior five years of financial history from the City's current system into the new platform, with reconciliation and control totals signed off by Accounting before cutover. Migration runs in a rehearsal pass followed by a final load, and the team works directly with Accounting and IT on file formats, timing and validation so the transition causes minimal downtime and operational impact. The proposal states the assumed source system, record volumes and file formats used to size the effort.

claims.text: The prior five years of data must be imported for history.

components.title: Implementation plan, schedule and go-live
components.description: A phased implementation plan and task sequence sized to reach go-live on July 1, 2026, aligned to the start of the City's fiscal year, with milestones for configuration, migration, parallel testing, training and cutover. The plan names key implementation personnel, describes support levels during implementation and for recurring licenses and services, and sets out the client engagement approach including the role of an account manager. Contingency is built into the schedule so a late contract award compresses scope rather than the go-live date.

claims.text: The City's stated go-live target is July 1, 2026, with the project starting soon after contract award and negotiation.

components.title: Training and change management
components.description: Personalized power-user training and manuals for the City's finance staff, plus at least one recorded training session and a written manual made available to all staff, delivered in person, virtually or as standard recordings by license level as the City prefers. Training is scheduled before go-live on configured data and repeated after cutover, and the recorded sessions and manuals stay with the City as reference material. The approach accounts for a small staff carrying full-time duties during the transition.

claims.text: The City's small staff and single vacancy mean training must fit around full-time operational duties.

components.title: Ongoing support, help desk and annual e-filing
components.description: Twelve months of post-implementation support included in the base price, covering a help desk with a ticketing system that prioritizes and tracks requests, named support hours, and escalation paths. The vendor pushes automated software updates and issues change notices so the City knows what changed and when, and provides annual 1099 and W-2 e-filing support each filing season. Support continues through annual contract renewals with the same account manager, and the proposal states response-time commitments so the City can score the technical support criterion.

components.title: Security, data protection and financial-condition assurance
components.description: A security documentation package for Attachment G describing the controls protecting the City's financial data: encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access, multi-factor authentication, segregation of duties, logging and monitoring, backup and recovery, and incident response, mapped to a recognized framework so the City can compare it to its expectations. The bid also supplies Attachment D certification of financial stability with an unqualified audit opinion and no liens or disqualifying litigation, signed by an authorized representative, and Attachment E proof of workers compensation and commercial general liability coverage.

components.title: Price proposal and cost transparency
components.description: Attachment A is completed as the price proposal cover sheet and references the specific tasks and deliverables in the RFP's scope of work. The price breaks out the implementation fee, recurring fees, license fees, and support costs during implementation separately from post-implementation, plus an estimate for any additional applications or vendors. The total price covers all materials, supplies and travel, reimbursable expenses are capped at a stated figure rather than left unlimited, and the total price proposal amount is stated as a single figure. The price is submitted as final and is not altered during clarification.

components.title: Proposal assembly, references and demonstrations
components.description: The bid team assembles the response in the RFP's required tab order within the page allowance, with a signed original hard copy and a digital copy emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov under the required subject line before the August 28, 2025 4:00 PM PST deadline. The package includes a completed Attachment F software abilities spreadsheet, license types by level of use, the account-number customization description, disclosure of any additional applications or vendors, and the availability of virtual product demonstrations. It carries at least three references for similar work with valid e-mail addresses and full contact detail, a local referral able to host an in-person demonstration, and firm qualifications and key personnel summaries.

claims.text: Proposals are due August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST, with finalist interviews on September 25, 2025 and award targeted for October 22, 2025.

assumptions.text: All six modules the City runs today, including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and purchase orders with approvals, are assumed to be required functionality of the new system and are replaced one-for-one.
Five users is assumed to be the licensed quantity at go-live, with additional named-user licenses priced as an option rather than included in the base.
July 1, 2026 is treated as a firm go-live commitment, with implementation assumed to begin within 30 days of the October 22, 2025 award target.
The twelve months of post-implementation support is assumed to start at go-live and to be included in the base price rather than priced as an option.

The five-year data migration is assumed to draw from the City's current Tyler Technologies Fund Balance system in its standard export formats, with the City supplying extracts and the vendor performing mapping and cleaning.
The reimbursable expense cap is assumed to be a respondent-proposed figure stated in Attachment A, set at a level covering travel for on-site training and cutover support.
The total price proposal amount is assumed to be the sum of the total price for all services and deliverables plus the capped reimbursable expenses, stated as one figure.
The Attachment F software abilities spreadsheet is assumed to match the functional scope described in the RFP's scope of work, and is completed against that scope pending the City's separate file.

The City's standard contract is assumed to be its General Contract Terms and Conditions without material deviation, so no exceptions are raised in the proposal and any concerns are raised as written questions by July 31, 2025.
Where the 30-day and 15-day financial-certification notice periods conflict, the shorter 15-day period to the Contract Lead is assumed to govern, with the City also notified within 30 days.
Insurance is assumed to be carried at limits customary for a municipal software and services contract, with certificates naming the City as additional insured, pending the City's stated limits.
Attachment G documentation is assumed to be accepted as a written control narrative mapped to a recognized security framework, since the RFP names no standard.
The account manager role is assumed to be a named, dedicated contact included in the base price rather than an optional or on-site resource.
The 20-page limit is treated as binding, with the cover letter and appendices kept within their separate allowances.
The hard copy is assumed to be delivered to the 33 S. Main Street address to be physically received by the 4:00 PM PST deadline, with the emailed copy sent before the same time.

risks.title: Attachment F spreadsheet not available, so the 45%-weighted scope response is built blind
risks.description: Attachment F ("Software Abilities and Requirements") is a separate Excel file the City must supply and the proposal must return completed, but it is not in the RFP package. The bid team must therefore guess the City's line-item functional requirements and price against them; if the real spreadsheet contains items the proposed platform does not cover, the bid is either non-responsive or needs unplanned configuration and third-party products after award. Because Tab 1 carries 45% of the score, a mis-scoped Attachment F also directly costs evaluation points.
risks.justification: The document is mandatory (R061) and holds solution requirements, yet it is listed as a separate attachment not included in the RFP; the solution itself admits it is completed against an assumed scope pending the City's file.
risks.mitigation: Request Attachment F in writing before the July 31, 2025 question deadline and state in the proposal that the response is completed against the RFP scope of work pending the City's file; hold a priced contingency for any line items outside the six named modules.

risks.title: City's standard contract and General Contract Terms not available before bidding
risks.description: The RFP makes all its terms enforceable contract conditions and bars modified terms in the proposal, yet the standard contract and the General Contract Terms and Conditions are only 'available upon request' and are not in the package. The bidder must accept unseen terms covering liability, indemnity, insurance and termination, and any objection raised in the proposal risks rejection.
risks.justification: R039 and R025/R026 make unseen terms binding and objections disqualifying, while the contract documents are missing; the solution assumes no material deviation without having read them.
risks.mitigation: Request the standard contract and General Contract Terms in writing before July 31, 2025; if not produced, state in the proposal that the bid is conditioned on review of those documents and raise any concerns as written questions rather than as proposal exceptions.

risks.title: July 1, 2026 go-live is a goal, not a fixed date, and the start date is undefined
risks.description: The RFP states July 1, 2026 as the City's goal and says work starts 'soon after' award, with award targeted for October 22, 2025 but no notice-to-proceed date. If award slips or negotiations run long, the roughly eight-month window to configure six modules, migrate five years of history, test and train compresses; the solution's answer is to cut scope rather than move the date, which risks an incomplete cutover at fiscal-year start.
risks.justification: The date is aspirational in the RFP and the start is undefined, yet the solution treats July 1, 2026 as a firm commitment and plans to absorb slippage by compressing scope.
risks.mitigation: State in the proposal that the schedule assumes a notice to proceed by a named date (for example mid-November 2025) and define in advance which scope items are deferred if award is later, so the City chooses the trade-off rather than the vendor.

risks.title: Hard-copy delivery and page-limit compliance could disqualify an otherwise strong bid
risks.description: The proposal must arrive as one signed original hard copy physically received at a Colfax address by 4:00 PM PST on August 28, 2025, alongside an emailed copy, and the RFP is unclear whether the PO Box and street address are alternatives and whether the 20-page limit is pass/fail. A courier delay or an over-length response could make the bid unevaluable regardless of its quality.
risks.justification: Late and FAX submissions are not evaluated and the page limit is stated as 'should' while the surrounding text says respondents are required to adhere; the solution assumes the street address and treats the limit as binding.
risks.mitigation: Ask the City which address to use and whether the hard copy must physically arrive by the deadline, then ship by tracked courier at least three business days early and hold the response to the page allowance with the cover letter and appendices in their separate budgets.

risks.title: Attachment G security documentation required but its standard and format are undefined
risks.description: Attachment G asks for documentation of financial-data protection and secure access controls, but the form is not in the package and no framework, format or scope is named. The bid team cannot tell whether a control narrative, a SOC 2 report or a certification will be accepted, so it may submit evidence the City scores as insufficient, or over-invest in documentation that is not what was wanted.
risks.justification: R102 is mandatory and Attachment G is a referenced document absent from the PDF, while the RFP names no standard; the solution's assumption that a narrative mapped to a recognized framework will be accepted is unverified.
risks.mitigation: Ask the City by July 31, 2025 which standard and format Attachment G requires, and submit a control narrative mapped to a recognized framework plus the current SOC 2 report as supporting evidence.

risks.title: Attachments A to E missing, so pricing, references, location and certification forms must be reconstructed
risks.description: Attachment A (pricing proposal), B (references), C (location of workers), D (financial condition certification) and E (insurance certification) are all referenced but supplied separately and absent from the RFP. The bid team must recreate the forms, risking a submission that is rejected as incomplete or that omits a required field, and cannot confirm the exact price breakout the City will score.
risks.justification: Five mandatory submission forms (R089, R084, R097, R098, R100) are missing from the package; the RFP requires all attachments to be populated and signed, and the solution already assumes it can recreate Attachment B.
risks.mitigation: Request the full attachment set with the written questions and, if not supplied, submit faithfully reconstructed forms with every field the RFP describes, flagging in the cover letter that the City's originals were not provided.

risks.title: Small City staff cannot carry their share of implementation and training
risks.description: The City has 11 full-time employees with one vacancy plus one part-time employee, and the solution relies on City Accounting and IT to supply extracts, validate data, sign off control totals and attend training. If City staff cannot free the time, milestones slip and the vendor absorbs rework; the RFP does not commit City resources or name a project sponsor.
risks.justification: The headcount is stated in the RFP and the solution itself notes the vendor must carry most of the workload, yet the plan still depends on City sign-offs and joint working sessions.
risks.mitigation: State in the proposal the City effort assumed per phase (named roles and hours), propose a single City project sponsor, and schedule training and validation sessions around the City's operational calendar.

risks.title: Conflicting 30-day and 15-day financial-certification notice periods
risks.description: R099 requires notice to the City within 30 days of any condition materially altering the financial certification, while R139 requires notice to the Contract Lead within 15 days of material changes to the same representations. Operating to the wrong clock after award could breach a contractual notice obligation, and the RFP does not define what counts as a material change.
risks.justification: The two requirements conflict on both the period and the recipient, and the certification does not define 'material change'; the solution resolves it by assumption rather than by the City's answer.
risks.mitigation: Ask the City which notice period and recipient govern, and until answered operate to the shorter 15-day period to the Contract Lead with a copy to the City.

risks.title: Five-year data migration sized on assumed source formats and volumes
risks.description: The RFP does not state the volume, format or cleanliness of the prior five years of history, nor who supplies and cleans the extracts. The solution assumes standard Tyler Technologies Fund Balance exports with the City supplying extracts and the vendor mapping and cleaning them; if the data is messier, larger or in non-standard formats, migration effort and reconciliation time grow and the go-live date is at risk.
risks.justification: R110 is mandatory and the RFP leaves volumes and formats undefined; the solution's sizing rests on an explicit assumption about the source system and export formats.
risks.mitigation: Ask the City for record counts, file formats and a sample extract before the deadline, and state in the proposal that the migration price covers a defined volume and format with re-pricing for material variance.

risks.title: Twelve months of post-go-live support priced into the base without a defined scope
risks.description: The RFP does not say whether the 12 months of support is included in the base price or optional, when it starts, or what service levels apply. The solution assumes it starts at go-live and is included in the base price, which puts a full year of help desk, update notices and annual 1099/W-2 e-filing support inside a fixed price the City will not let the bidder revise during clarification.
risks.justification: R114 is mandatory but its pricing basis is undefined, and R033 bars price changes during clarification, so an under-priced support year cannot be corrected later.
risks.mitigation: Ask the City to confirm the support period's start and whether it is base or optional, and price it explicitly as a separate line with stated support hours, response targets and an assumed ticket volume.

risks.title: Reimbursable expense cap and total price structure left to the bidder's guess
risks.description: The RFP requires a capped reimbursable figure and a total price proposal amount but gives no ceiling, no methodology and no explanation of how the total relates to the services total plus the cap. The solution assumes a respondent-proposed cap covering on-site travel and treats the total as the sum of services plus cap; if the City expected a different construction, the price sheet is scored as non-responsive or the cap under-recovers travel costs.
risks.justification: R088, R124 and R125 are mandatory but the cap basis and the relationship between the three amounts are undefined, and the solution resolves both by assumption.
risks.mitigation: Ask the City by July 31, 2025 whether a maximum cap or methodology is prescribed and how the total price proposal is composed; state the construction used in Attachment A explicitly so the City can see the arithmetic.

risks.title: Insurance limits and additional-insured terms unstated, so coverage cannot be priced or confirmed
risks.description: Attachment E requires proof of workers compensation and commercial general liability coverage, but the RFP states no limits, additional-insured requirements or certificate form. The solution assumes limits customary for a municipal software contract; if the City's actual requirements are higher, the bidder either fails a mandatory submission item or absorbs unplanned premium.
risks.justification: R100 is mandatory and the coverage requirements are open-ended ('including, but not limited to'), while the solution's insurance position rests on an explicit assumption pending the City's stated limits.
risks.mitigation: Ask the City for the required limits and endorsements before the deadline, and submit certificates at customary municipal limits naming the City as additional insured, with a note that limits will be conformed to the contract.

referenced_documents.name: Attachment F
referenced_documents.section: Tab 1: Response to Project Goals and Scope
